cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with message "r must not be null"
cases.description: Calling addRecord with a null argument should immediately throw an IllegalArgumentException.

input.value: SOARecord with name = new Name("other.example.com.") and origin = new Name("example.com.")

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with message containing "SOA owner other.example.com. does not match zone origin example.com."
cases.description: When the record type is SOA but its owner name does not equal the zone origin, addRecord must reject the record.

input.value: A Record with name = new Name("outside.com.") where zone origin = new Name("example.com.")

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with message containing "name outside.com. is absolute and not a subdomain of example.com."
cases.description: If the record's name is not a subdomain of the zone origin, addRecord must reject it.

input.value: A Record with name = new Name("www.example.com.") and type = Type.A

cases.expected: Zone contains a new RRset for name www.example.com. with exactly one record (the added A record). No exception thrown.
cases.description: When there is no existing RRset for the given name/type, addRecord should create a new RRset and store it in the zone.

input.value: A Record with name = new Name("mail.example.com.") and type = Type.A

cases.expected: The existing RRset for mail.example.com./A now contains the newly added record in addition to any previous records. No SOA handling occurs.
cases.description: When an RRset already exists for the name/type and the record is not a SOA, addRecord must simply add the record to the existing RRset.

input.value: SOARecord with name = zone.getOrigin() (e.g., example.com.) and new serial number

cases.expected: The previous SOA record is removed from the RRset, the zone's internal soaRecord field is updated to the new SOARecord, and the RRset now contains only the new SOA record.
cases.description: When an existing RRset is found and the incoming record is a SOA, addRecord must delete the old SOA from the RRset, replace the zone's soaRecord reference, and add the new SOA.

input.value: SOARecord with name = zone.getOrigin() (e.g., new Name("example.com.")), serial = 2023100101, mname = new Name("ns.example.com."), rname = new Name("hostmaster.example.com."), refresh = 3600, retry = 600, expire = 604800, minimum = 86400

cases.expected: No exception thrown. Zone.soaRecord is set to the added SOARecord. A new RRset for name example.com. with type SOA exists containing exactly one record (the added SOA).
cases.description: When the zone has no existing SOA, adding a valid SOA record should store it, update the internal soaRecord field, and create an RRset containing only that SOA.

input.value: NSRecord with name = zone.getOrigin() (e.g., new Name("example.com.")), target = new Name("ns1.example.com.")

cases.expected: No exception thrown. A new RRset for name example.com. with type NS is created and contains the added NSRecord. Zone.soaRecord (if previously set) remains unchanged.
cases.description: Adding a non‑SOA record whose name equals the zone origin should be allowed; the record is stored in its own RRset and does not affect the SOA handling.

input.value: A Record with name = new Name("dup.example.com."), address = 192.0.2.1

cases.expected: First call: RRset for dup.example.com./A created with one record. Second call (same record): No exception; RRset still contains exactly one record (duplicate is ignored).
cases.description: Adding the same Record object twice should not create duplicate entries inside the RRset; the RRset size remains unchanged after the second addition.

input.value: A Record with name = new Name("host.deep.sub.example.com."), address = 198.51.100.42

cases.expected: No exception thrown. A new RRset for name host.deep.sub.example.com. with type A is created containing the record. The subdomain check passes because the name is a subdomain of the zone origin (example.com.).
cases.description: Verifies that the method correctly recognises multi‑level subdomains as valid members of the zone.

input.value: A Record with name = new Name("multi.example.com."), address = 203.0.113.5

cases.expected: First call creates RRset with one record. Second call with a different A record (address = 203.0.113.6) adds to the same RRset, resulting in exactly two records in the RRset. No exception thrown.
cases.description: When an RRset already exists for a name/type, adding another record of the same type should increase the RRset size accordingly.

input.value: A Record with name = new Name("www.example.com.") and type = Type.A

cases.expected: NullPointerException (thrown when zone origin is null during subdomain validation)
cases.description: If the Zone object's origin field is null, the call to name.subdomain(origin) (or name.equals(origin)) triggers a NullPointerException. The method should not swallow this error.

input.value: SOARecord with name = zone.getOrigin() (e.g., new Name("example.com.")), serial = 2024010101, mname = new Name("ns.example.com."), rname = new Name("hostmaster.example.com."), refresh = 3600, retry = 600, expire = 604800, minimum = 86400

cases.expected: NullPointerException (thrown inside rrset.deleteRR(soaRecord) because soaRecord is null)
cases.description: An empty RRset of type SOA is manually added to the zone (using Zone.addRRset) without setting the internal soaRecord field. When addRecord is invoked with a new SOARecord, the method finds the existing RRset, attempts to delete the previous SOA via rrset.deleteRR(soaRecord), and crashes because soaRecord is still null.
